# Maintenance and Troubleshooting {#sec-maintenance}

Start fault finding with sample identity, preparation, power, calibration state and mechanical fit. Preserve the original data and settings before changing hardware or reinstalling software. A correction that changes optics, assay conditions or blank state must be followed by the appropriate calibration and control checks.

## Routine care

Remove the sample tube after use. Keep the optical compartment dry and free of dust, and inspect tube seating, filter retention, cables and the light shield before a batch. Wipe the exterior without allowing liquid into electronics or filter pockets.

Disconnect USB and the optional battery before opening the enclosure or moving boards. Handle filters by their edges and use suitable optical tissue or a clean optical blower. Do not scrape detector surfaces or use abrasive material on filter coatings. Check material and coating compatibility before using a cleaning solvent.

Keep boards supported and strain-relieve cables so connectors are not carrying mechanical loads. If a battery is swollen, damaged or unusually hot, take it out of service. Record maintenance that might change the measurement response.

## Startup and connections

| Observation | Checks | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Dark display or no startup | Power switch, USB supply, cable and optional battery | Test with a known-good USB data cable; inspect for a short with power disconnected before reinstalling software |
| No computer drive | Data-capable cable, USB port and reset mode | Confirm whether `CIRCUITPY` or the UF2 boot drive is intended |
| Boot drive appears during file maintenance | Reset double-click was too fast | Reset once and use the slower safe-mode sequence |
| Missing configuration or module | Root-directory layout and complete release contents | Back up the drive; repeat the documented clean installation if files are incomplete |
| `TSL2591 not found` | Upstream adapter, mux supply, downstream cable and detector connection | Inspect connections without power; restart after correction |
| `Need exactly one TSL2591` | Number of matching sensors on scanned branches and configured channel | Restore the documented single-detector setup or correct the configured channel |
| LED board absent from I2C scan | Board is a fixed-current driver without an I2C address | This absence is expected; check supply and LED polarity if it remains dark |
| Fatal application error | Error type, stage and serial traceback | Record the error before resetting; correct the underlying cause |

Do not hot-plug internal connectors. Confirm pin identity and supply polarity from the actual assembly and design records rather than wire colour alone. The unresolved cable/connector details in the build review require physical confirmation.

## Signals and sample handling

| Observation | Possible cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Blank changes with room light | Gap at tube opening, filter pocket, seam or cable exit | Check the closed optical path and refit the shield; recheck before calibration |
| Persistently saturated signal | Missing/displaced emission filter, light leak or excessive sample fluorescence | Inspect the optics; predilute the original sample when its concentration is above range |
| Low response from a known standard | LED polarity/supply, alignment, filter identity, detector position or reagent/preparation error | Verify the optical sequence, preparation and reference tube before changing gain |
| High within-cycle spread or drift | Bubbles, incomplete mixing, movement, changing temperature or unstable tube seating | Correct an identified cause and repeat; retain the earlier result |
| Tube sticks or shifts the module | Print debris, poor fit or damaged tube | Remove the obstruction or replace the part; do not force the tube |
| Unexpectedly high sample result | Identity error, contamination, wrong volume or incompatible calibration | Check records and make a fresh independently prepared assay |
| Negative blank-corrected estimate | Sample signal below the retained blank or baseline mismatch | Inspect the blank check and controls; retain the raw estimate and apply the reporting convention |

The detector's FULL and IR channels contribute to the calculated VIS signal. Inspect all three when diagnosing unusual behavior. A small technical SD does not rule out wrong concentration, contamination or a preparation error.

## Calibration and controls

| Observation | Meaning or check | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Calibration disappears after START | Ordinary blank replacement invalidates the two-point model in RC2 | Repeat the complete two-point calibration if replacing the blank was intended |
| Stored two-point calibration should be retained | A fresh blank check is needed without replacing state | Measure the blank-check tube with A under a traceable ID and evaluate it with QC |
| `PROV` displayed | Historical/provisional multipoint state is active | Return to the intended routine two-point workflow; do not accept provisional model output as routine calibration |
| Standard signal invalid | Nonpositive or insufficient blank-corrected signal | Check standard identity, pipetting, reagent and optics; prepare and calibrate again |
| `CV`, `SNR` or `SAT` in calibration review | Firmware warning, even if saving is possible | Investigate and obtain an acceptable calibration/control before sample analysis |
| Independent control fails | Calibration, blank or assay conditions may be unsuitable | Hold affected results; investigate and repeat QC and the necessary calibration/assays |
| Limits unavailable after recalibration | New two-point calibration resets the saved blank-limit estimates | Establish suitable limits for that calibration or apply a documented accepted method boundary |

Do not use the historical example slope or blank counts as universal pass/fail thresholds. Maintain control targets and acceptance intervals for the actual instrument and assay. A failed control is a reason to investigate, not a reason to widen its acceptance interval after measurement.

## Files and data recovery

| Observation | Check | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Concentrations display but CSV is unchanged | USB data-host connection at startup and logging setting | Restart on standalone power and verify newly saved test rows |
| Calibration save fails | Device write access and available storage | Back up data, restore the documented write arrangement and repeat calibration/save |
| Wrong sample names | Live-screen selection, configuration list and saved index | Select the correct ID before A; document any already mislabelled rows without overwriting evidence |
| CSV rows split into extra columns | Commas or line breaks in sample IDs | Use simple IDs without CSV separator/quote characters; preserve and document the damaged source file |
| Apparent time jumps | Runtime clock restarts or several sessions appended | Reconstruct sessions from batch notes; `t_s` is not UTC |
| Multipoint JSON rejected during development | Model label, field names and schema mismatch | Check the documented RC2 contract; v7.3 export is not directly compatible |

Multipoint import is an optional development capability. It is not required to characterize a series in the Calibration Suite or to analyze routine samples with two-point calibration. Avoid changing unrelated configuration files to repair an import problem.

## Return the instrument to service

1. Record the fault, affected batch interval, corrective work and any replaced part.
2. Recheck mechanical fit, optical shielding and the intended sensor settings.
3. Verify blank behavior and use the correct blank action for the calibration route.
4. Recalibrate after a change that invalidates the active calibration, and repeat relevant characterization for a new configuration.
5. Measure an independently prepared control and verify logging.
6. Resume reportable samples only when the applicable checks pass; repeat affected samples where required.

The screw schedule remains a deferred build task until the instrument can be inspected. Do not turn a provisional screw entry into a confirmed maintenance instruction without that check.
